extracted.intended_audience: journalists, public relations professionals, researchers, and general readers interested in media practices and embargoes
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the norms, uses, requirements, and consequences surrounding news/press embargoes: what they are, how they're arranged, typical terms (dates/conditions), parties involved, and common practices in journalism, PR, and scientific publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a news/press embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: A request or requirement by a source that the information or news provided by that source not be published until a certain date or certain conditions have been met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by businesses (product announcements), medical journals, and government officials; the media is given advance knowledge so reports can be prepared to coincide with the announcement and meet press time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo timing and conditions must be explicit
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoes hold that information must not be published until a specified date/time or until particular conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include synchronization across time zones for coordinated releases (IMF briefing embargoed until 10:30 a.m. Washington time) and journal embargoes tied to the issue cover date (JAMA embargo until 15:00 Central Time on the day before the cover date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance access in exchange for secrecy (review embargoes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review embargoes grant early access to content or products (video games, hardware, films) to reviewers on the condition that review results remain secret until the embargo lifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to prevent inaccuracies in reviews, avoid harming sales at launch, and allow discovered flaws or bugs to be fixed prior to public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo arrangement type and consent (gentlemen's agreements vs unsolicited embargoes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoes are usually arranged in advance as 'gentlemen's agreements', but publicists sometimes send embargoed press releases unsolicited hoping newsrooms will respect the date without prior agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase 'For Immediate Release' at the top of a press release indicates the information is not embargoed; unsolicited embargoed material may lack mutual consent and can cause confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for breaking an embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: If the embargo is broken, the source may retaliate by restricting access to further information for that journalist or publication, which is typically considered a serious breach of trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaking can be accidental (miscommunication) or intentional (to scoop competitors). Example: Piers Morgan intentionally breaching a BBC embargo to tweet details early and being criticized by other journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: reduce inaccuracy and allow better reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoes theoretically reduce inaccuracies in reporting of breaking stories by removing the incentive to rush and by giving journalists time to research background and prepare more comprehensive coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They enable production of 'backgrounders' alongside the story and let journalists verify context and details rather than cutting corners to publish first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical/scientific journal embargo practices (Ingelfinger rule context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Major medical journals apply embargoes to health-related news about upcoming articles; journalists receiving advance copies agree not to publish until the embargo time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals (e.g., NEJM, JAMA, The Lancet) may mail advance copies during the week before publication and prepare press releases and news videos. Rationale: enables doctors and scientists to analyze studies before public release and supports accurate commentary; critics argue some embargo use is profit-driven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lockup procedures for sensitive government/economic announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters may be held in a 'lockup' before release of important government announcements (budgets, statistics) where they can prepare stories but are not permitted to file until after the official announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lockups aim to prevent insider trading and synchronize reporting. Examples: Canadian and Australian budget lockups; US practices (e.g., Federal Reserve) are uncertain or vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo as a tool of source influence and ethical implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoes are one mechanism by which sources influence media presentation; alongside 'on background', 'not for attribution', and controlled access, they affect how information is disseminated and framed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalistic ethics govern how reporters should respond to attempts to influence coverage; embargoes raise questions about transparency and the balance between cooperation and editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoes can be imposed or observed for reasons other than source control (self-censorship)
rubrics_metrics.description: An embargo may be instigated by parties other than a source (e.g., to protect safety or ongoing investigations), reflecting self-censorship rather than source-imposed secrecy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: suppression of news about kidnapped reporter David Rohde until his safe return—an embargo-like suppression prompted by media organizations themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticisms and potential misuse of embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargo systems, particularly in medicine and publishing, may be criticized as serving journals' profit or status motives rather than purely public-interest reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly critiques and case studies (cited further reading) question whether embargoes are used to attract better papers, expand circulation, or lure advertising, and document consequences when embargoes distort reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical markers and signals in press releases regarding embargo status
rubrics_metrics.description: 'For Immediate Release' signals that material is not embargoed; absence of such phrasing or explicit embargo instructions indicates an embargo may apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicists and newsrooms should look for explicit embargo instructions, agreed terms, and timestamps; unsolicited press releases claiming embargo status should be treated cautiously unless prior agreement exists.
